analysis:
Market context: Broad indices have bounced from April lows with selective participation. The screened universe shows a healthy mix of confirmed uptrend-basing setups (FDS, PYPL, ROP, FTNT) and mixed/sideways names still seeking direction. Starting from 100% cash with no legacy positions is an advantage — we can be selective.

Strategy: Target Stage 1→2 transitions in the lower half of the 52-week range, where fundamentals are solid but price has already absorbed most of the bad news. Three names stand out for combining (a) strong quality metrics, (b) undemanding forward valuations, and (c) confirmed uptrend-basing technicals with positive SMA50 slopes.

PYPL: The cheapest quality fintech in the screened list (fwd P/E 8.7x, PEG 0.91) with $3.3B FCF and 25%+ ROE. Sitting at 29% of 52w range with SMA50 slope accelerating at +3.2% — momentum is turning. Revenue growth is modest but the re-rating from 9x earnings is asymmetric.

FDS: FactSet is a narrow-moat data franchise trading at fwd P/E 11.6x — historically cheap. At only 13% of its 52-week range (lowest in the list), it has absorbed significant institutional selling. SMA50 slope is positive; the basing pattern is intact. ROE 28%, op margin 30%, FCF yield attractive.

ROP: Roper Technologies is a serial acquirer of niche vertical-software businesses — among the highest-quality compounders in the S&P 500. At 15% of its 52w range with fwd P/E 14.9x, it trades at a significant discount to history. SMA50 slope +0.5% confirms the base is building. Down 18.7% from SMA200 = recovery runway.

All three positions sized so a full stop-out costs ~1.3-1.5% of equity each. Combined portfolio heat ≈4.5%. Cash remaining ≈25% (buffer for adds or new setups).

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $50.00 or better on any intraday pullback; acceptable up to $51.50. The SMA50 is sloping up strongly (+3.2%/20d) — do not chase if it gaps above $53.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: PayPal is a payments network with 25%+ ROE, $3.3B annual FCF, and $6.4B operating cash flow trading at a forward P/E of 8.7x and PEG of 0.91 — deeply discounted relative to intrinsic value. The new management team (Alex Chriss) is executing on margin expansion and checkout improvements. At $45B market cap vs $3.3B FCF that is a ~7.3% FCF yield for a durable payments franchise. Technical: UPTREND basing at 29% of 52w range. SMA50 slope is the steepest positive in the screened list at +3.2% over 20 days, confirming buyers are returning. Price is 7.5% above SMA50 — not extended. Still 14.5% below SMA200, so recovery runway is meaningful.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) stop at $47.67 is hit intraday on closing basis; (2) price rallies to $65 target — reassess thesis and trim; (3) revenue growth prints negative for two consecutive quarters, signaling secular deterioration; (4) time stop: if flat/down in 6 months with no earnings inflection, reassess. Trail stop to breakeven once +10% gained.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $222.00 or any pullback toward the 50-day SMA (~$217-220 zone). Current price $224 is only 3% above SMA50 — acceptable entry. Do not pay above $228.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: FactSet is a subscription-based financial data and analytics platform with strong competitive moat (switching costs, workflow dependency). ROE of 28%, operating margin 30%, FCF of $590M, and a forward P/E of just 11.6x (PEG 1.09) — this is the cheapest it has traded in years on an earnings basis. The selloff from $466 to $189 (now $224) has been driven by rate-sensitive multiple compression, not fundamental deterioration. Revenue is still growing at +7%. Technical: At only 13% of 52-week range — the lowest of all 30 candidates — the bulk of institutional selling appears complete. Confirmed UPTREND with basing pattern. SMA50 slope is positive (+0.5%). The risk/reward of entering near the range floor with trend confirmation is asymmetric.
trades.exit_plan: Stop at $210.30 (1.75x ATR below entry). Target $275 = partial SMA200 recovery. Thesis break: if FactSet loses a major data contract or subscription churn accelerates meaningfully. Time stop: reassess in 9 months if no progress toward SMA200. Add on confirmed breakout above SMA200 if thesis intact.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $353.00 or pullback toward SMA50 (~$354). Current price is essentially at the SMA50 — textbook basing entry. Avoid chasing above $365.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: Roper Technologies is one of the highest-quality serial acquirers in the S&P 500, focused on niche vertical-software and data businesses with recurring revenue and high switching costs. Forward P/E of 14.9x with 11.3% revenue growth is attractive for a business of this quality — historically it trades at 22-28x. FCF of $2.2B on a $36.6B market cap is a 6% FCF yield. Op margin 27.2% reflects the asset-light model. Technical: At only 15% of 52-week range (second lowest in the list), UPTREND basing with SMA50 slope +0.5%. Down 18.7% from SMA200 — the recovery toward fair value and mean-reversion toward SMA200 (~$430+) provides a clear multi-month path. ATR is only 2.5%, making stop placement tight relative to upside.
trades.exit_plan: Stop at $339.69 (1.75x ATR). Target $420 corresponds to ~SMA200 recovery. Thesis break: if Roper announces a large dilutive acquisition that destroys capital allocation discipline, or if free cash flow conversion deteriorates. Trail stop to $355 breakeven once +8% in profit. Candidate for LTCG extension if thesis intact past 12 months.
